name: Klampt joint-waypoint planning example
summary: Guarded Python 3 Klampt example that loads a world, edits joint waypoints, plans a trajectory, saves resources and visualizes the result. It also defines optional Cartesian IK-goal and closed-loop planning branches, disabled by default.

license.scope: Upstream BSD-3-Clause declaration for the selected Python example only. Its pinned copyright line is incomplete: Copyright (c) 2018, with no holder. Attribution remains unresolved; no holder from the separate core repository is substituted. Models, meshes, configurations, controllers and third-party dependencies are outside this review.

requirements.python: Python 3.x (upstream directory declaration; exact version untested)
packages: PyOpenGL and PyQt6 for visualization as declared by the reviewed core README
system: Working GUI and graphics environment for interactive waypoint editing and visualization
Configured world/robot model and adjacent assets from the upstream examples checkout
requirements.notes: Run from Python3/demos/plan or supply an explicit world path. The default loads ../../../data/robots/jaco.rob; this Jaco discovery label does not establish model compatibility. Default SBL planning uses restart/shortcutting, active DOFs auto, a 500-iteration limit and a nominal 10-second budget. CLOSED_LOOP_TEST and PLAN_CARTESIAN_TEST are both zero by default. SIMPLIFY_TYPE=ConvexHull changes geometry; fidelity and collision behavior are unverified. Direct waypoint-editor feasibility rejection is disabled. Execution can write planningtest.configs resources and test.path and visualize a path for 60 seconds. Model/mesh bytes and licenses were not reviewed; package/native-library combinations, planning success and timing were not tested.

invocation.notes: Upstream guarded main after configuring dependencies, world assets, GUI and intended file-output locations.
